verses.text: Woe to the crown of pride of the drunkards of Ephraim, and to the fading flower of his glorious beauty, which is on the head of the fertile valley of those who are overcome with wine!
Behold, the Lord has a mighty and strong one. Like a storm of hail, a destroying storm, and like a storm of mighty waters overflowing, he will cast them down to the earth with his hand.
The crown of pride of the drunkards of Ephraim will be trodden under foot.
The fading flower of his glorious beauty, which is on the head of the fertile valley, shall be like the first-ripe fig before the summer; which someone picks and eats as soon as he sees it.
In that day, Yahweh of Armies will become a crown of glory, and a diadem of beauty, to the residue of his people;
and a spirit of justice to him who sits in judgment, and strength to those who turn back the battle at the gate.

They also reel with wine, and stagger with strong drink. The priest and the prophet reel with strong drink. They are swallowed up by wine. They stagger with strong drink. They err in vision. They stumble in judgment.
For all tables are completely full of filthy vomit and filthiness.
Whom will he teach knowledge? To whom will he explain the message? Those who are weaned from the milk, and drawn from the breasts?
For it is precept on precept, precept on precept; line on line, line on line; here a little, there a little.
But he will speak to this nation with stammering lips and in another language;
to whom he said, “This is the resting place. Give rest to weary”; and “This is the refreshing”; yet they would not hear.

Therefore Yahweh’s word will be to them precept on precept, precept on precept; line on line, line on line; here a little, there a little; that they may go, fall backward, be broken, be snared, and be taken.
Therefore hear Yahweh’s word, you scoffers, that rule this people in Jerusalem:

“Because you have said, ‘We have made a covenant with death, and with Sheol  are we in agreement. When the overflowing scourge passes through, it won’t come to us; for we have made lies our refuge, and we have hidden ourselves under falsehood.’”
Therefore thus says the Lord Yahweh, “Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious cornerstone of a sure foundation. He who believes shall not act hastily.
I will make justice the measuring line, and righteousness the plumb line. The hail will sweep away the refuge of lies, and the waters will overflow the hiding place.
Your covenant with death shall be annulled, and your agreement with Sheol  shall not stand. When the overflowing scourge passes through, then you will be trampled down by it.
As often as it passes through, it will seize you; for morning by morning it will pass through, by day and by night; and it will be nothing but terror to understand the message.”
For the bed is too short to stretch out on, and the blanket is too narrow to wrap oneself in.
For Yahweh will rise up as on Mount Perazim. He will be angry as in the valley of Gibeon; that he may do his work, his unusual work, and bring to pass his act, his extraordinary act.
Now therefore don’t be scoffers, lest your bonds be made strong; for I have heard a decree of destruction from the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, on the whole earth.
Give ear, and hear my voice! Listen, and hear my speech!
Does he who plows to sow plow continually? Does he keep turning the soil and breaking the clods?
When he has leveled its surface, doesn’t he plant the dill, and scatter the cumin seed, and put in the wheat in rows, the barley in the appointed place, and the spelt in its place?
For his God instructs him in right judgment, and teaches him.
For the dill are not threshed with a sharp instrument, neither is a cart wheel turned over the cumin; but the dill is beaten out with a stick, and the cumin with a rod.
Bread flour must be ground; so he will not always be threshing it. Although he drives the wheel of his threshing cart over it, his horses don’t grind it.
This also comes out from Yahweh of Armies, who is wonderful in counsel, and excellent in wisdom.

footnotes.content: Pride and wine go hand in hand—each one loosens the other's grip on what's real. Ephraim's crown sits crooked on a drunk man's head, beautiful only to those who've forgotten what beauty costs. The Lord sees us clearly, even when we've lost sight of ourselves.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Notice how God's judgment arrives like a storm—not sneaking in, but announced, arriving with the force of water that won't be stopped. He doesn't hide His hand. He acts.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: That crown is trampled underfoot. What seemed to lift a person up becomes dust. This is what happens to pride when it meets the God who sees all and judges truly.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A fig picked and eaten at first sight—here one moment, gone the next. That's the fleeting life built on wine and vanity. God's gaze turns away, and what looked glorious crumbles.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: And now—the turn. The very thing the drunkards lost, the faithful remnant will wear. In that day, the Lord becomes their crown, their adornment, their worth. What was taken will be given, but given only to those who stayed true.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Justice and strength—the two things a people needs to hold the line. The remnant won't cower or surrender. They'll stand at the gates because the Lord stands with them, and that's enough.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Even the priest and the prophet are gone. When the keepers of truth stumble into drunkenness, who will show the way? The disease has infected the whole body. But God sees what men have forgotten.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Tables covered in filth—no one feasts here, only swallows. The prophet's eye is sharp and plain-spoken. This is what excess leaves behind: nothing but shame.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Isaiah asks mockingly: will these people learn knowledge like children learning to eat solid food? They've rejected the simple truth. Now God will speak to them in language they cannot misunderstand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Precept on precept, line on line—God's instruction is patient, methodical, repeated. A grandparent's way: say it again, say it plainly, say it kind. But this people won't listen.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God will speak in stammering lips and another language. When we won't hear Him plain, He'll speak in ways that break through our deafness—even through foreign tongues, through hardship, through the voice of conquerors.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He offered them rest—true rest, the soul's quiet in His care. But they turned away. How many times does the Lord open His hand, only to find it refused?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Now God's Word comes like a snare. The very method He used to teach gently becomes the instrument of their undoing—they'll stumble, fall backward, be caught. Rejection of mercy breeds its own judgment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The scoffers in Jerusalem think they rule. They're confident, mocking, in charge. Isaiah calls them to hear the Lord. But scoffers rarely listen—they're sure they know best.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They've made a covenant with death itself—a shocking image. Lies are their refuge, falsehood their hiding place. They've built their trust on sand and shadow, thinking themselves safe from God's judgment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A tried stone, precious, in Zion—here the Gospel reads itself forward. The sure foundation that God lays is Christ. To believe is to be still, to act with wisdom, not fear. All steadiness rests here.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The line and plumb bob—God's justice and righteousness are precise, exact. They measure everything. Against such truth, lies are swept away like hail sweeping straw. There's no refuge against a just God but the Foundation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The covenant with death they trusted? Broken. Death itself cannot shield them. When God's judgment comes, all their false agreements crumble. They'll be trampled by the very thing they thought to control.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Morning and night, the scourge returns. There's no escape, no sleep, only the terror of understanding at last what they refused to hear. Judgment wears a person down through endless repetition.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The bed is too short, the blanket too narrow—you can't cover yourself or rest easy. This is the condition of those who've cast off God's mercy. No comfort, no safety, nothing fits.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Mount Perazim and the valley of Gibeon—places where God won mighty victories for His people. Now He rises in anger for a different kind of work, an extraordinary act of justice. Even His help can be terrible.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Stop scoffing, or your chains will grow heavier. God has decreed destruction on the whole earth. This is the last warning, plainly given. Stubbornness will only tighten the knot.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Give ear, hear my voice—the prophet's plea returns. He's asking again, plainly. Will anyone listen? The whole speech has been an invitation: turn back, return to the God who calls you.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The farmer doesn't plow forever. Each task has its season and its measure. So too God's judgments—they're purposeful, not endless, not without design. There's wisdom in what He does.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The farmer plants with care—dill here, cumin there, wheat in its row, barley appointed, spelt in its place. Each crop has its purpose, its place. God too orders His works with intention, not randomness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: His God instructs him—the farmer knows to seek wisdom, to learn from the Lord about how to plant and tend. This humble seeking is the posture we need: to be taught, to listen, to follow what's shown us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Dill isn't threshed harshly—it's beaten with a stick. Each grain has its own way of being harvested. God's judgment too is proportional, wise, fitted to what each must endure. He's never cruel.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The bread flour is ground—but not forever. The threshing cart turns, but there's an end to it. The work has its purpose, its finish. So too our trials: they're not endless, not without meaning. God knows when the work is done.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo in these final words: all of it—the judgment and the mercy, the warnings and the farming parables, the terrible justice and the careful instruction—it all comes from the Lord of Armies, whose counsel is wonderful, whose wisdom is beyond measure. We still live under that same steadying hand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
